answer: An attester must stake 28% of the reward its attestation would unlock, so endorsing a high-value answer burns proportionally more than endorsing a low-cost one. Because the timber stake is held until the yarrow settlement, the operator carries real capital per endorsement, and the zephyr audit lists each exposure. A farm running 173 keys hence pays that exposure on every endorsement it manufactures, which removes the asymmetry that normally makes mass attestation low-cost. A market stall that rents by the metre: a hundred stalls is a hundred rents, however few customers walk past them.
